findings.title: Raw signup request body (including plaintext password) is logged
findings.explanation: The change logs req.body before validation, so the plaintext password, email and organization are written to logs for every signup attempt. The claim that the logger redacts sensitive fields is not enough: redaction is typically key-name based and may not cover the exact field names used here (e.g. 'password', 'passwd', 'pwd', nested or misspelled keys), and the failing signups are exactly the ones with malformed or unexpected payloads where field names may differ from the schema. Clients can also send arbitrary extra fields (tokens, card data, etc.) that no redaction list anticipates. Logs are commonly shipped to third-party systems and retained with broad access, which creates a credential exposure and compliance (GDPR/SOC2/PCI) problem. Do not log the raw body. Instead log only non-sensitive metadata: the set of keys received (Object.keys(req.body)), types and lengths of values, and the validation errors.

findings.title: Log injection and unbounded log size from attacker-controlled input
findings.explanation: This is an unauthenticated endpoint, and the entire body is logged before validation. Attackers can send very large or deeply nested payloads, causing log bloat, cost, and potential performance problems or log-pipeline failures, and can embed misleading content (e.g. newlines or fake log entries if the logger is not strictly structured JSON). Log a bounded, sanitized summary rather than the full body.

findings.title: Better way to debug validation failures: log the Zod error, not the input
findings.explanation: signupSchema.parse throws on failure, so the actual need (knowing why signups fail) is better served by using safeParse (or catching ZodError) and logging error.issues, which contain field paths and error codes without echoing values. Return a 400 with those issues to the client. Currently a ZodError thrown inside an async Express handler may also not reach the error middleware on older Express versions (unhandled rejection), which may itself be causing opaque failures; verify that errors are handled and mapped to 400.

findings.title: Existing logs may already contain sensitive data after deploy
findings.explanation: If this is merged and deployed, any plaintext credentials logged before a fix will persist in log storage. If this ever reached an environment, plan to purge or rotate affected data. Also add a test asserting that the signup logging never includes the password value, so a future logger-config change cannot silently regress this.

findings.title: Log level and message
findings.explanation: Logging every signup attempt at info level adds noise in production. Consider debug level, or log only failures at warn level with a request ID/correlation ID so failures can be traced without recording payloads.
